question.worked_solution:
First, we decompose all of the terms into their various factors. The $3a(a-b)$ in the numerator becomes $3\cdot a\cdot (a-b),$ and the $9(a-b)$ in the denominator becomes $3\cdot 3\cdot (a-b).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3a(a-b)}{9(a-b)}=\frac{3\cdot a\cdot (a-b)}{3\cdot 3\cdot (a-b)}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we cancel out all the pairs of common factors in the numerator and denominator. In this case, there is one pair of $3$'s and one pair of $(a-b)$'s.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3a(a-b)}{9(a-b)} & =\frac{3\cdot a\cdot (a-b)}{3\cdot 3\cdot (a-b)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{3}\cdot a\cdot \cancel{(a-b)}}{\cancel{3}\cdot 3\cdot \cancel{(a-b)}} \\  & =\frac{a}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the expression simplifies to $\frac{a}{3}.$
